desc: Implement a factorial table up to 100 with values capped at a limit > 10^15 (e.g., 10^18) to prevent overflow and enable safe comparisons with k.

Write a count function: given remaining odd count o, even count e, and the parity required for the next position (or "free" if no previous element), return the number of valid alternating completions — 0 if infeasible, fact[o]*fact[e] if next parity is forced, or 2*fact[o]*fact[e] if free and o == e.
Compute the total number of alternating permutations for n (handle even n: 2*(n/2)!²; odd n: odd!*even!), and return [] if k exceeds it.

Implement the greedy construction loop: maintain available odd and even numbers in sorted order; at each position determine the required parity (opposite of previous, or free at start), iterate candidates of that parity in increasing order, compute block size via the count function, subtract from k when skipping, and pick the candidate whose block contains k.

Handle the starting-position special case: when n is even, both parities are allowed at position 0, so consider all candidates 1..n in lexicographic order with appropriate block counts; when n is odd, only odd candidates are allowed.
Test against the three provided examples plus edge cases (n=1, n=2, k=1, k equal to total count, k > total) to verify correctness.
